The combination of 2-methoxyestradiol (2ME) with chemotherapy is being explored as a potential treatment for certain cases of human ovarian cancer. Specifically, 2ME has been shown to enhance the antiproliferative activity of chemotherapeutics at pharmacologically relevant concentrations.

In one study, patients with refractory metastatic breast cancer who received the combination of 2ME and chemotherapy had tolerable tolerance, indicating that this approach may offer a new clinically relevant treatment regimen for hormone-dependent cancer. Another study found that in patients treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (chemotherapy before surgery), the use of 2ME did not alter the frequency or topographic distribution of lymphadenectomy (a surgical procedure to remove lymph nodes).

However, it is essential to note that more research is needed to fully understand the effects of this combination on ovarian cancer treatment. Additionally, while 2ME has shown promise in some studies, its effectiveness and safety have not been established in all cases.

In summary, the current evidence suggests that the combination of 2-methoxyestradiol with chemotherapy may offer a new treatment approach for specific patients with hormone-dependent ovarian cancer. However, further research is required to confirm these findings and to establish the efficacy and safety of this combination for various types of ovarian cancer.
